# Recipes: end-to-end workflows

Ten task walkthroughs with real command lines and typical outputs. Examples
use a hypothetical `my_game` crate and entity id `4294967299`; substitute
what `brp world list-components` / `brp world query` report for your app.
Every command is one shot: JSON on stdout, exit 0 on success (see
`reference/troubleshooting.md` when it is not).

## 1. Probe the connection

```console
bevy_copilot status
```

```json
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:15702/",
  "state_dir": "/var/folders/.../T/.bevy_copilot",
  "reachable": true
}
```

`reachable` comes from a live `rpc.discover` probe. The command exits 0
even when the app is down — check the field, not the exit code. Run this
first; if `reachable` is false, nothing else will work.

## 2. Find entities by component

```console
bevy_copilot brp world query --data '{"components": ["my_game::Health"]}'
```

```json
[
  { "entity": 4294967299, "components": { "my_game::Health": { "value": 100.0 } } },
  { "entity": 4294967300, "components": { "my_game::Health": { "value": 80.0 } } }
]
```

Add `--filter '{"with": ["my_game::Player"]}'` to narrow the match, or
`"option": ["my_game::Mana"]` inside `--data` for may-have components. See
`reference/conventions.md` for the full payload grammar. For looser
phrasing, `brp debug nl-query --query 'entities with my_game::Health where
my_game::Health.value < 50'` parses a small natural-language subset into the same
call.

## 3. Read and change component values

```console
# Read two components of one entity
bevy_copilot brp world get-components 4294967299 --components my_game::Health,my_game::Mana
```

```json
{
  "components": {
    "my_game::Health": { "value": 100.0 },
    "my_game::Mana": { "value": 50.0 }
  },
  "errors": {}
}
```

```console
# Set Health.value to 42, then re-read to confirm
bevy_copilot brp world mutate-components 4294967299 --component my_game::Health --path value --value 42.0
bevy_copilot brp world get-components 4294967299 --components my_game::Health
```

Mutations print `null` on success and take effect on the live app
immediately — there is no undo outside `brp debug experiment` sessions.
Whole-component writes use `brp world insert-components 4294967299
--components '{"my_game::Health": {"value": 42.0}}'`.

## 4. Spawn and despawn entities

```console
bevy_copilot brp world spawn-entity --components '{"my_game::Health": {"value": 100.0}}'
```

```json
{ "entity": 4294967301 }
```

Save the returned id; `brp world despawn-entity 4294967301` removes the
entity and its children.

## 5. Watch for changes

```console
bevy_copilot brp watch get-components 4294967299 --components my_game::Health --frames 3
```

```jsonl
{"components": {"my_game::Health": {"value": 100.0}}, "errors": {}}
{"components": {"my_game::Health": {"value": 99.0}}, "errors": {}}
{"components": {"my_game::Health": {"value": 98.0}}, "errors": {}}
```

Frames stream as JSONL, one compact object per line, shaped like the
matching non-watch call. ALWAYS bound a watch with `--frames <N>` and/or
`--max-ms <MS>` — unbounded it streams until the pipe closes. Add
`--skip-first true` to swallow the initial-state frame and wait for the
first actual change (`--skip-first true --frames 1`). `brp watch list-components` also has an initial state. Event observation has
no initial-state frame: use `brp watch observe --event my_game::Ping --frames 1`
to receive the first real event batch without `--skip-first`.

## 6. Capture a screenshot

```console
bevy_copilot brp extras screenshot --path /tmp/shot.png
```

Writes the primary window to `/tmp/shot.png`. Needs a windowed app running
`bevy_copilot_extras`. Useful modifiers: `--camera <id>` (capture that
camera's viewport), `--entity <id>` (crop to an entity's bounds),
`--padding <px>` (margin around the crop).

## 7. Drive the app with synthetic input

```console
bevy_copilot brp extras send-keys --keys KeyW,Space
bevy_copilot brp extras type-text --text "hello"
bevy_copilot brp extras click-mouse --button left --x 400 --y 300
bevy_copilot brp extras move-mouse --x 640 --y 360
bevy_copilot brp extras drag-mouse --button Left --start 100,100 --end 300,300 --frames 30
```

Combine with recipe 6 (screenshot before/after) to build see-act-verify
loops: screenshot, send input, screenshot again, diff visually.

## 8. Discover and call app-specific methods

Apps can register their own BRP methods (e.g. `my_game/reset_level`).
There is no dedicated subcommand for them — use the generic passthrough:

```console
# 1. List every advertised method
bevy_copilot brp rpc discover

# 2. If the app publishes a tool catalog, read it for params schemas
bevy_copilot brp extras list-agent-tools

# 3. Call the method with verbatim JSON params
bevy_copilot brp rpc execute my_game/reset_level --params '{"level": 3}'
```

`rpc execute` self-gates on discovery: an unadvertised method fails before
any POST, so a typo cannot poke the app.

## 9. Record, replay, and checkpoint a QA scenario

CLI invocations are one-shot: a recording started with
`brp debug record --action start` dies with the process. The workflow
therefore splits across surfaces:

```console
# Record with the MCP server (its state lives for the server's lifetime):
#   bevy_copilot mcp  ->  brp_debug_record start  ->  mutate via brp_* tools
#   ->  brp_debug_record stop   (journal saved to <state dir>/journal.jsonl)

# Replay the saved journal from the CLI (works one-shot):
bevy_copilot brp debug replay
```

Replay re-applies the journaled mutations and returns `{applied, remapped,
entity_map}`. Known envelope targets are remapped; component/custom payloads
require explicit `entity_paths` JSON pointers in journal entries. Numeric business
fields stay unchanged. Checkpoint restore spawns fresh entities without rewriting
payload references. It does not remove the old entities or revert the current
world. Use a controlled fixture and inspect the returned entity map before
continuing; do not treat restore as undo. Checkpoints persist to the state dir,
so capture and restore work across CLI invocations:

```console
bevy_copilot brp debug checkpoint --action capture --name before_fight --components my_game::Health
# ... break things ...
bevy_copilot brp debug checkpoint --action restore --name before_fight
```

## 10. Check performance and scan for anomalies

```console
# Frame diagnostics from the app (needs bevy_copilot_extras)
bevy_copilot brp extras get-diagnostics

# Scan a fresh snapshot: NaN/null Transform leaves, missing-component rules
bevy_copilot brp debug anomaly --components bevy_transform::components::transform::Transform

# Latency profile of a synthetic load: p50/p95/p99, total time, ops/sec
bevy_copilot brp debug stress --scenario '{"kind": "spawn_many", "count": 1000}'
```

The `nan_transform` anomaly rule is how you catch NaN/inf poisoning: those
floats arrive as `null` over the wire. The `perf_spike` rule needs
in-memory frame samples, so it only fires in MCP server mode, not one-shot
CLI runs.
